text: A Python run starts one deadline watchdog and arms it for each module step, where every step used to start an interpreter of its own (#856). A step sends it the step's timeout and a pipe only that step holds; the watchdog starts the deadline when it answers armed, kills the runner past it as before, and answers disarmed when the step closes the pipe. A run whose watchdog dies or answers anything else fails with no accepted observations, and an explicit stop ends the watchdog with the run. Each step keeps a deadline of its own, enforced from a second interpreter, and a process the application forks still keeps it armed. What goes is an interpreter start per step: about 14 ms natively on the development machine and more under emulation, which a long exploration paid at every step. ask3d's statue gate went from 492 s to 457 s.
